beats.text: In this town, a T-rex the size of a skyscraper lives at the end of my street.
beats.visual: Day lighting. Low camera on main street: the kid narrator (tan skin, spiky brown hair, red cap, blue hoodie) waves in front of his house. The camera tilts up past the rooftops and keeps going to a giant blocky green T-rex towering over the houses, ten times taller than the street lamps, blinking huge googly eyes.

beats.text: His name is Biscuit. Twelve years ago, he walked out of the dinosaur park, sat down, and never left.
beats.visual: Wide shot from the park: Biscuit plods in past a 'DINOSAUR PARK' arrow sign at the edge of town and plops down behind the clock tower. Every house hops up off the ground, the camera shakes, and townspeople peek out of their windows.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: Kid in the middle of the street, huss face, slam pose. Biscuit's giant head leans down curiously behind him. Quick punch-in on each HUSS.

beats.text: His arms are way too short, so the whole town takes care of him.
beats.visual: Close-up of Biscuit's tiny arms wiggling uselessly at his chest, trying to reach an itch. Cut to the crowd below looking up (think pose), holding brooms and ladders.

beats.text: Mr. Okafor brushes his teeth with a street sweeper. Firefighters scratch his back with a ladder.
beats.visual: Biscuit's jaw opens wide like a garage door. Mr. Okafor (dark skin, mustache, overalls) stands on the pink tongue scrubbing a tooth with a giant brush. Cut to a red fire truck with its ladder raised, scratching Biscuit's back while his huge leg thumps the ground like a happy dog.

beats.text: Every time somebody says walk, his tail wags so hard it knocks over the water tower.
beats.visual: A townsperson in the park points and mouths 'walk'. Biscuit's tail whips across the skyline and knocks over the water tower, which tips over with a splash of blue cubes. Everyone ducks (surprised pose).

beats.text: And every morning, he fetches the school bus. Full of kids. Covered in drool.
beats.visual: Biscuit trots into the town square with the yellow school bus in his mouth and sets it down gently. The door opens and dripping kids stumble out (sweat faces, shrug poses) as blue drool drips from the roof.

beats.text: Then yesterday, he got the hiccups.
beats.visual: Close-up of Biscuit's face. His eyes go suddenly wide and the frame freezes.

beats.text: Every hiccup bounced the whole town ten feet into the air.
beats.visual: Wide shot of the street: Biscuit jolts, and every house, lamp post and townsperson pops ten feet into the air and slams back down. Heavy camera shake, then it happens again.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The kid hangs mid-air above the street, arms flailing (surprised pose, huss face), with houses floating behind him. Another bounce on each HUSS.

beats.text: Grandpa's teeth landed in a bird's nest. The bakery landed on the library.
beats.visual: Grandpa (white beard, glasses) in shock with no teeth. Pan up to the pigeon sitting proudly on his false teeth in a nest on a lamp post. Cut to the bakery house stacked on the library roof, with the baker on top shrugging.

beats.text: The only cure for hiccups? Scare it.
beats.visual: Town square. Grandma (grey bun, glasses, purple cardigan) at the stage mic, pointing dramatically up at Biscuit while the crowd nods.

beats.text: The mayor yelled boo. The marching band played their loudest note. He just yawned.
beats.visual: The mayor (top hat, sash) cups his hands on the stage and yells. A marching band blasts gold tubas up at Biscuit. Biscuit gives an enormous slow yawn, then hiccups again and everyone bounces.

beats.text: So I dragged the barbershop mirror to the top of the clock tower.
beats.visual: The kid hauls a tall silver-framed mirror up the outside of the clock tower, sweating (sweat face, determined). At the top he heaves it up right in front of Biscuit's gigantic eye.

beats.text: He leaned down, looked into it, and screamed so loud the clouds left town.
beats.visual: Biscuit leans in and his reflection appears in the mirror. His eyes go huge, his jaw drops and he ROARS. A shockwave ring pushes all the clouds off-screen, hats fly off the crowd, and the camera shakes hard.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The kid clutches the mirror on top of the clock tower with a huss face. Biscuit tumbles backwards into the park in slow motion while the crowd below cheers and confetti flies.

beats.text: The hiccups stopped. But then I realized something.
beats.visual: Quiet. Biscuit sits in the park staring at the mirror propped against the clock tower, tilting his head like a confused dog. The kid looks up at him (think pose).

beats.text: He had never seen himself before. For twelve years, he thought he was a golden retriever.
beats.visual: Quick warm-tinted flashback montage: Biscuit wagging his tail, tongue out, fetching the bus, leg thumping during the back scratch.

beats.text: Now he's hiding behind the mountain and won't come out.
beats.visual: Dusk lighting. Only Biscuit's two huge sad eyes and the tip of his tail peek over the big hill behind town. Townspeople walk away below (walkSad).

beats.text: So today, the whole town dressed up as dinosaurs, so he wouldn't feel weird.
beats.visual: Next day. The whole town lines up at the foot of the mountain in green dinosaur hoods with cone spikes and arms tucked in tiny, doing dance poses. Biscuit peeks out and his tail starts to wag.

beats.text: It totally worked. Except Grandma's costume is so good, now he's scared of Grandma.
beats.visual: Grandma steps forward in an enormous, terrifyingly realistic dinosaur costume with glowing red eyes and a clacking jaw, and roars. Biscuit yelps, leaps behind the clock tower and covers his face with his tiny arms, trembling.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: Grandma in costume strikes a slam pose, lifts the dino mask to show a huss face and winks at the camera. Biscuit shakes as he peeks out from behind the clock tower.

notes: The golden-retriever reveal is the real twist, but the softer Grandma-costume ending buries it. Cut the costume ending and finish on the retriever line plus one callback shot: Biscuit wagging behind the mountain in a giant dog collar, fetching the bus again. Also drop the marching band and the bakery-on-library props to lighten the build, and rename the T-rex, because homey-1's cat is also called Biscuit.

Give the kid a stated reason for the mirror ('What scares a T-rex? Another T-rex.'). The scream then reads as a clever plan that works for the wrong reason, and the golden-retriever reveal recasts it. That reveal is already well set up by the walk, fetch and leg-thump beats.

The T-rex rig (hinged jaw, segmented wagging tail, wiggling arms, thumping leg) carries every shot and takes a full day by itself. Cut the teeth-in-the-nest, bakery-on-the-library and marching-band beats: they won't read at phone size and add 5+ props. Use that time and the freed narration to plant why the mirror would scare him, for example Biscuit flinching at the dinosaur on the DINOSAUR PARK sign early on. Also rename him, because homey-1's cat is also called Biscuit.

ranked.title: Sunrise
ranked.logline: In this town the sun won't come up until somebody makes Grandma Bea laugh, so every morning the whole town lines up at the stage to try. One Tuesday nothing works, and the town is stuck in the dark until noon, until one kid tries something nobody has ever done: asking Grandma to tell HER joke.
ranked.twist: Grandma laughs so hard at her own terrible joke that the sun bounces into the sky; she only wanted someone to laugh with. Then her grumpy brother Walt moves in next door. The moon only rises when HE laughs, he has never laughed in his life, and Uncle Dave, whose knock-knock joke has never worked, is already knocking on his door.

beats.text: In this town, the sun won't come up until somebody makes Grandma Bea laugh.
beats.visual: Town square before dawn, deep blue sky. Tiny Grandma Bea (white bun, pink cardigan, round glasses) sits in a rocking chair on the stage under a banner that reads MAKE BEA LAUGH. On the horizon a giant sleeping sun with closed eyes peeks over the hills.

beats.text: Eighty years ago, baby Bea giggled, and the sun popped up for the very first time.
beats.visual: Flashback at dusk: a little bassinet. A giggle sparkle pops above it, and the giant sun boings up over the hills for the first time. Townspeople in old-fashioned hats gasp.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The narrator kid (yellow raincoat, headphones around neck) pops up in front of the stage, huss face, pointing at the sleeping sun.

beats.text: So every morning at five, the whole town lines up at the stage.
beats.visual: A long line of about 30 extras in pajamas with sleepy faces snakes across the dark town square up to the stage. Someone holds a mug.

beats.text: Rule one: no repeat jokes. Rule two: no tickling. That's cheating.
beats.visual: The kid holds up fingers to camera. Cut to a man in the line with wiggling fingers sneaking toward Grandma. A big red DENIED stamp slams down on him.

beats.text: Mr. Okafor juggles frozen fish. Sunrise, six-oh-two.
beats.visual: Mr. Okafor (beard, chef apron) juggles three light-blue box fish on stage. Grandma Bea laughs and the sun rises over the hills behind them.

beats.text: The mayor once fell off the stage. Best summer ever.
beats.visual: The mayor (top hat, sash) waves, steps backward and tumbles off the edge of the stage. Grandma laughs hard and the sun blazes extra bright.

beats.text: Uncle Dave tells the same knock-knock joke every single day. It has never worked. Not once.
beats.visual: Uncle Dave (big mustache, bowtie, hopeful grin) knocks on the air on stage. Grandma Bea stares back, neutral face. Crickets of silence. A counter ticks to 0 FOR 4,380.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The kid face-palms then does huss face beside a deflated Uncle Dave, who shrugs.

beats.text: Until Tuesday. Grandma Bea stopped laughing.
beats.visual: Dark stage. Grandma Bea sits with crossArms and a sad face. Joke after joke fails in front of her. The sleeping sun on the horizon doesn't move.

beats.text: Six AM. Nothing. Nine AM. Still dark. By noon, even the pigeons went back to bed.
beats.visual: The clock tower at quiet night with its hands spinning. Street lamps glow. The pigeon on the clock tower ledge tucks its head under its wing and falls asleep.

beats.text: We ate lunch by flashlight. Mr. Okafor ran out of fish.
beats.visual: The park table at night: a family eats sandwiches by the light of glowing flashlights. Mr. Okafor stands nearby holding an empty bucket upside down, sad face.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The kid in the middle of the dark town square, shocked huss face. The camera spins around him, street lamps flicker, and the whole crowd panics in the background.

beats.text: Everyone tried. Pies. Clowns. Grandad did the worm across the whole stage.
beats.visual: Quick montage on stage: a cream pie flies across, someone in a party hat and red nose does a dance, then Grandad (grey beard, cap) slides across the stage flat on his belly doing the worm. Grandma stays stunned.

beats.text: Nothing. Then I noticed something. Everyone was telling HER jokes. Nobody ever asked for hers.
beats.visual: The kid in think pose at the side of the stage. Camera slowly pushes in on Grandma Bea, alone in her chair, looking a little lonely while the crowd argues about who goes next.

beats.text: So I sat down next to her and said, 'Grandma, tell me a joke.'
beats.visual: The kid sits on the stage edge beside the rocking chair. The crowd goes quiet. Grandma Bea turns her head slowly, surprised face.

beats.text: Why didn't the sun go to college? It already had a million degrees!
beats.visual: Grandma Bea in Grandma's own voice, grin face, pointing finger up at the sleeping sun as she delivers the punchline.

beats.text: It was terrible. And she laughed so hard she snorted.
beats.visual: Grandma Bea doubles over in laugh pose and laugh face, rocking chair tipping back. The kid starts laughing too. A big SNORT stamp pops.

beats.text: The sun shot up so fast it bounced.
beats.visual: The giant sun opens its eyes and rockets up from behind the hills, bounces once in the sky, then settles. Lighting snaps from night to bright day. Camera shake, birds scatter.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: Sunny town square: the whole town in pajamas cheers and dances. Grandad crowd-surfs across the crowd. The kid does huss face on the stage next to Grandma, who is still giggling.

beats.text: Turns out she didn't need a show. She just wanted someone to laugh with.
beats.visual: Warm close shot: the kid and Grandma Bea sit together on the stage edge in the sunshine, both laughing. The smiling sun glows behind them.

beats.text: But today, her brother Walt moved in next door. The moon only rises when HE laughs.
beats.visual: Dusk. A moving van parks next to Grandma's house. Walt (long grey beard, flat cap, brown coat) stands on the porch in crossArms with a squint face. Behind the hills, a giant frowning moon waits.

beats.text: Walt has never laughed in his life. And Uncle Dave is already knocking.
beats.visual: Uncle Dave, hopeful grin, knocks on Walt's front door. Walt stares down at him without blinking. The kid turns slowly to the camera with sweat face.

notes: Line 1 is charming but a 12-year-old won't stop scrolling for it. Cold-open on the crisis instead: "It's noon. It's pitch black. Because Grandma Bea won't laugh," with the dark town and the pigeon asleep. Then rewind to the rules. That puts the stakes and the strange visual in the first two seconds.

Set up the closing twist. Early on, show a night sky that never has a moon ('We haven't had a moon since Grandma's brother moved away.') so Walt's arrival pays something off instead of being a bolted-on sequel hook. Also fix the rule clash: Uncle Dave repeats his joke daily despite 'no repeat jokes', so stamp him an explicit 'special permit'.

There is a hole in the moon logic: if the moon only rises when Walt laughs and Walt has never laughed, the town has never had a moon. Rewrite the line as 'Walt's old town hasn't seen the moon in eighty years. Tonight, ours didn't come up either.' Show a black sky with the frowning moon stuck behind the hills, so the twist doesn't contradict every earlier night.

ranked.title: Nugget
ranked.logline: Ever since the dinosaur park's fence fell over, every kid in town rides a dinosaur to school. I ride a chicken. When I enter her in the Great Dino Race, the whole town laughs, right up until the race turns into a twelve-dinosaur pile-up.
ranked.twist: Nugget wins by slowly walking past the pile-up and ringing the bell with her face. Then she sits on top of the clock tower and lays an egg bigger than the clock tower itself. Every dinosaur runs screaming back into the dinosaur park and fixes the fence themselves, and the egg starts cracking with a very, very deep 'BAWK'.
ranked.caption_hook: everyone laughed at my chicken. then she laid an egg.
new_props: Nugget the chicken: small white body (box/sphere), red box comb and wattle, orange cone beak, stick legs, flappy box wings. Kid-sized, so the kid's feet touch the ground when he rides her
teal triceratops: box body, round frill disc, three cone horns, thick tail
purple raptor 'Sprinkles': slim upright body, long snout, sickle claws
long-neck dinosaur: big body, tall cylinder neck whose head is above the rooftops, can tip over sideways
T-rex (shared rig with the Biscuit build)
dinosaur park fence: tall wooden plank wall plus a gate with a 'DINOSAUR PARK' sign. It falls over in the flashback and gets fixed at the end
'THE GREAT DINO RACE' banner and a chalk start line across main street
starter flag for the mayor
big gold bell at the top of the clock tower
clipboard sign-up sheet
giant white egg (huge sphere, scaled tall) with a zigzag crack and glowing light leaking out
crumbling clock tower top (box chunks that fall away)
'KEEP OUT' sign, hammer and nailed boards on the fixed fence
dust cloud (grey spheres) for the race start
sets: town main street (day) with houses and street lamps, used as the race course
town square with stage and big banner (day)
clock tower exterior, stairs and top bell platform
dinosaur park gate and fence at the edge of town
town square at night with the giant egg

beats.text: In this town, everybody rides a dinosaur to school. Except me.
beats.visual: Day lighting, main street. Kids ride past on blocky dinosaurs: Priya on a teal triceratops, Big Darnell on a purple raptor, and a long-neck whose head bobs above the rooftops. The kid narrator (light brown skin, curly black hair, yellow jacket, glasses, backpack) stands alone on the sidewalk.

beats.text: I ride Nugget. Nugget is a chicken.
beats.visual: The camera pans down to show the kid sitting on a small white chicken with his sneakers flat on the ground. Nugget blinks at the camera.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The kid on Nugget, huss face, cheer pose. Nugget flaps her wings while the dinosaurs behind them stare blankly. Punch-in on each HUSS.

beats.text: Ten years ago, the dinosaur park's fence fell over, and they all moved into town.
beats.visual: Warm-tinted flashback: the tall plank fence with the 'DINOSAUR PARK' sign tips over with a crash. Dinosaurs stroll out onto main street past the clock tower, one drinks from the fountain and the long-neck peeks into a second-floor window.

beats.text: Priya rides a triceratops. Big Darnell has a raptor named Sprinkles. The mailman rides a long-neck and delivers to the roof.
beats.visual: Quick character cards, each with a name tag: Priya (ponytail, pink sash) waves from her triceratops. Big Darnell (tall, sunglasses, chain) rears up on Sprinkles the raptor. The mailman (cap) sits on top of the long-neck and drops letters down a chimney.

beats.text: And every single day, they all laugh at me.
beats.visual: Town square. A crowd of extras and dinosaurs point and laugh at the kid on Nugget (laugh poses). Kid has a sad face and Nugget looks at her feet.

beats.text: Then came the Great Dino Race. First one to ring the clock tower bell wins.
beats.visual: The town square banner reads 'THE GREAT DINO RACE' and the mayor (top hat, sash) is on the stage. The camera tilts up to the big gold bell glinting at the top of the clock tower.

beats.text: I signed up Nugget. The whole town laughed so hard the long-neck fell over.
beats.visual: The kid signs a clipboard at the stage with Nugget tucked under his arm. The crowd erupts laughing, and the long-neck laughs so hard it tips sideways onto a house with a crunch.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The kid, determined face, crossArms pose, with Nugget sitting on his head. The long-neck lies across a squashed house behind them, legs in the air.

beats.text: Three. Two. One. GO!
beats.visual: Start line across main street. Twelve dinosaurs stomp and snort in a row, with tiny Nugget at the end. The mayor drops the starter flag.

beats.text: Twelve dinosaurs exploded off the line. Nugget just stood there, pecking at a crumb.
beats.visual: The dinosaurs blast off in a huge grey dust cloud and the camera shakes. The dust clears to show Nugget alone at the start line, calmly pecking one crumb, while the kid holds his head (think pose).

beats.text: Then Sprinkles tripped on the triceratops' tail.
beats.visual: Slow motion: the raptor's foot catches on the triceratops' tail and Big Darnell's sunglasses fly off. Everything freezes for a beat.

beats.text: The triceratops crashed into the stage. The stage launched the mayor. The mayor landed on the T-rex.
beats.visual: Chain reaction with whip-pans: the triceratops plows into the stage, which flips up like a seesaw and launches the mayor through the air (top hat spinning). He lands on top of the T-rex's head.

beats.text: And the T-rex sat on everybody.
beats.visual: The confused T-rex sits straight down on the whole pack of dinosaurs. A big dust puff and camera shake.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: A wide shot of the dinosaur pile-up blocking main street, legs and tails sticking out and stunned faces. The kid in the foreground with a huss face.

beats.text: Twelve dinosaurs. One giant pile. Nobody could move.
beats.visual: Overhead shot of the tangled pile. A long-neck head waves weakly from the bottom.

beats.text: And Nugget? Nugget just walked. Slowly. Right past them.
beats.visual: Slow motion: Nugget strolls calmly past the pile, one step at a time, and every dinosaur's eyes follow her.

beats.text: Up the steps. Up the tower. And she rang the bell with her face.
beats.visual: Nugget hops up the clock tower steps. At the top she headbutts the giant gold bell, which swings with a huge DONG.

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The kid sprints into the town square with both arms up (cheer) as confetti falls. Nugget stands on top of the clock tower with her wings spread like a champion.

beats.text: Nobody was laughing now.
beats.visual: The crowd and the dinosaurs stare up at the tower in total silence, jaws dropped (shocked faces).

beats.text: Then Nugget sat down on top of the clock tower and laid an egg.
beats.visual: Close on Nugget at the top of the tower. She fluffs up, wiggles, squints hard (squint face) and settles down.

beats.text: The egg was bigger than the clock tower.
beats.visual: A gigantic white egg swells out from under Nugget. The clock tower top cracks and crumbles under it, and the egg drops into the town square, dwarfing every dinosaur. The camera tilts up, and up, and up.

beats.text: Every dinosaur in town ran screaming back into the dinosaur park and fixed the fence themselves.
beats.visual: All twelve dinosaurs scramble screaming through the dinosaur park gate. The triceratops slams the gate, the raptor hammers boards onto the fence, and the long-neck holds up a 'KEEP OUT' sign.

beats.text: Now the egg is cracking. And something inside just went...
beats.visual: Night lighting. The kid and Nugget stand beside the colossal egg in the empty town square as a jagged crack zigzags across it with glowing light leaking out.

beats.text: BAWK.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up on the glowing crack. The line is spoken by a very deep, pitched-down extra character voice. The whole town shakes and street lamps flicker.

beats.text: In a really, really deep voice.
beats.visual: The kid slowly turns to the camera (sweat face) while Nugget puffs out her chest proudly (smug face).

beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The kid in a slam pose with a huss face as the giant egg wobbles behind him and the pigeon flaps away in a panic.

notes: The giant egg comes out of nowhere. Plant one early clue: the T-rex flinches and steps back every time Nugget clucks in the opening street shot, so the egg reads as a reveal and not random. Cut the field from twelve unique dinosaurs to four hero dinos plus reused copies so the pile-up can actually be built.

Set up the ending. In the opening and race beats, show the dinosaurs quietly scared of Nugget: the T-rex steps around her, and Sprinkles hides when she clucks. Then the giant egg and the stampede back to the park pay off a clue. Give the passive narrator one active move too: he lays a crumb trail up the clock tower steps, using the pecking already set up at the start line.

As written this needs 4+ unique dinosaur rigs, 12 racers with riders and a seesaw chain reaction, which is too much for a day. Build one shared quadruped body with swappable heads and necks (frill and horns, long neck), give only the T-rex its own rig, and cut the race to 5 dinosaurs. Also drop the HUSS run after the sign-up: the script has 5 runs, over the 2–4 cap.
